symbols.name: draw_text
symbols.prototype: void draw_text(Canvas *canvas, const char *text, const Point *pos, int grey, int a8_unknown)
evidence: Whole body: font = get_font(2); draw_text_with_font(canvas=A4, font, text=B4, pos=A6, B6, A8). So it is draw_text_with_font with the default font 2.

264 call sites. B4 is a C string: the page titles (e.g. "SYSTEM INFO" 0xC16C8B64 via draw_page_title), and the global buffer 0xC1504360 that the caller at 0xC1561764 fills by copying a string and appending an integer (radix 10).
A6 points to two ints {x, y}: built on the stack at 0xC15617F8 as {9, 83} and at 0xC15D4234 as {x + 30, y - 1}; the page title uses the global at 0xC16D3500.

B6 is a 4-bit grey level (0 black .. 15 white): constants at the 264 call sites are 15 (82 sites, e.g. track and page names), 7, 5, 1 and 0; draw_text_with_font turns it into a byte passed by reference, and draw_text_impl writes it into pixel nibbles. A8 is 1 at almost every site; 0 at a few ("LOADING...", "ASSIGNED"), 3 at one. Meaning not yet known.
Correction 2026-11-10: 0xC16E3500 -> 0xC16D3500 (mis-decoded MVKH high halves; recomputed from the code's MVK/MVKH pairs).

symbols.name: draw_text_with_font

evidence: Argument order taken from draw_text, which forwards its own arguments shifted by one register pair with get_font(2) inserted as B4.

symbols.name: draw_text_impl
symbols.prototype: void draw_text_impl(Canvas *canvas, Font *font, const char *text, const Point *pos, const uint8_t *grey, int b8_unknown)
evidence: Called only through draw_text_with_font's thunk in the traced paths.

Ghidra decompile (noisy: circular-addressing artefacts): walks text bytes, handles '\n' (10) specially, looks glyphs up through tables in the font object (font+8, font+0xC), and writes *grey << 4 or *grey into a nibble of a byte (masks 0xF0/0x0F): a 4 bits-per-pixel framebuffer, two pixels per byte.
objdump decodes parts of this function inconsistently; read it in Ghidra's listing, not objdump.

symbols.name: MainDelegate::dispatch_control_switch
evidence: Reached from MainDelegate's ControlSwitchDelegate vtable (base offset 28) through the thunk 0xC154C198 (this -= 28).

Calls the receiving controller's vtable slot 4 (offset 16), i.e. ApplicationController::handleControlSwitchMessage. Routing: if g_modal_controller (B14+864) is non-null the event goes to it, else to g_current_controller (B14+860) followed through the child pointer at +8 to the innermost controller. Verified as a true virtual call (vptr load, slot load, branch).

Message layout as read here: 64-bit switch bit set at +0, 16-bit event code at +8 (bytes 8-9). With code 1 and the bit set equal to exactly one of bits 16, 17, 18, 24, 25, 31 (octave left, up, right, left, down, octave right in the g_control_switch_state map) it is handled on a separate path (not read further); other codes branch away early (0xC154C18C). Controllers' slot 4 handlers read the bits at +4 and the code at +12, i.e. they receive the message behind a 4-byte header (the dispatcher builds {3, ...} on its stack).

Bit usage over all slot 4 handlers matches the g_control_switch_state map: the most tested single bits are 23 (OK, 60 handlers) and 30 (CLR, 58); bit 9 (right selection) is tested by the rename / save-as pages, whose right selection button is OK in the manual. Handlers act on code 1 (presumably press; other codes not identified). Open: AppTuner and AppSystemInfo close on bit 26 (rec in the map) or CLR, which is unexpected for REC; their manual screens show 'return' on the left selection button.

Producer found: control_switch_poll sends code 1 = pressed and code 0 = released (single-bit messages, queued via post_control_switch); control_switch_repeat_tick sends auto-repeats (code 1, +10 = 2) directly to this dispatcher. Bit 26 is still open (the raw bit numbering comes from the scanner's hardware source, not read).

symbols.name: MainDelegate::dispatch_keypad_0
evidence: KeyPadDelegate vtable (base offset 40) entry 0, via 0xC154C2A8. Calls the controller's vtable slot 8 (offset 32). Routing: if g_modal_controller (B14+864) is non-null the event goes to it, else to g_current_controller (B14+860) followed through the child pointer at +8 to the innermost controller. Verified as a true virtual call (vptr load, slot load, branch).

Slot 8 receives a pointer to the message: word +0 = event kind, word +4 = pad index. AppDrumPadColor (0xC163BC38) and AppDrumPadNoteNumber (0xC162E594) act only when kind == 1, then store the pad index as the page's selected pad (this+16); selecting on kind 1 suggests 1 = pad pressed (inferred, not proven). Overridden by 40 of 177 ApplicationController descendants.

After the controller, the dispatcher passes the message to keypad_release_bookkeeping (0xC15D45A4), which returns at once for kind != 0 and, for kind 0, resets the pad's entries in per-pad tables (e.g. stores -1): kind 0 = released, kind 1 = pressed.
Producer: pad_sensor_update sends g_pad_event here; the message also carries the velocity at +8 (0 on release). The UI readers seen so far ignore it.

symbols.name: MainDelegate::dispatch_keypad_1
evidence: KeyPadDelegate entry 1, via 0xC154C3AC. Calls the controller's vtable slot 9 (offset 36). Producer: pad_sensor_update calls this entry when pad_hold_update reports that the most recently pressed pad has been pressed hard (raw > 2800) for 60 samples; the third argument is the pad index, not a message. Only HomeModeController overrides slot 9; what it does there is not read.

The hard-press hold is not described in the r2 reference manual (no hold or hard-press gesture for pads); it is an undocumented home-screen feature. HomeModeController's handlers (0xC151D5C8 for slot 9, 0xC151D484 for slot 10) were not decoded.

symbols.name: pad_sensor_update
symbols.prototype: void pad_sensor_update(PadSensor *self, int pad, int raw)
evidence: Returns at once if self+124 (the KeyPadDelegate) is null. Per-pad state word at self+4*pad (0 idle, 1 down), per-pad release counter at self+60+4*pad.

Press: pad idle and raw >= 800. The first such sample (any pad) is kept in g_pad_first_raw with g_pad_first_count = 1; on the next one pad_velocity(self, raw, g_pad_first_raw) gives the velocity, state = 1, g_pad_event = {1, pad, velocity} goes to delegate slot 0 (A4 = delegate, B4 = self, A6 = &g_pad_event), pad_hold_start(self+132, pad) runs and g_pad_first_count returns to 0. Release: pad down and raw < 100 for 4 calls in a row (any raw >= 100 clears the counter): state = 0, g_pad_event = {0, pad, 0} to delegate slot 0, and the hold tracker is reset if it was tracking this pad (pad_hold_current_pad).

While down and not yet released, pad_hold_update(self+132, pad, raw) runs; a result of 1 calls delegate slot 1 and 2 calls slot 2, both as (delegate, self, pad). The control flow uses branches in branch delay slots (one packet at the first target, then the second), read packet by packet from the objdump listing; Ghidra's decompile of this function is wrong.
Runs in the ADControllerUART task (task_loop -> parse -> MainDelegate::on_pad_analog), so pad events are delivered in task context.

symbols.name: g_midi_input_delegate
evidence: DP + 1116. Read by midi_in_uart_enable / midi_in_usb_enable and stored into the input ports' delegate field.

symbols.name: g_midi_usb_gate

symbols.name: g_midi_uart_gate

symbols.name: midi_set_thru

symbols.name: MIDI::MIDIStreamUART::task_loop
evidence: TaskHandler entry (thunk 0xC1620E24 subtracts 20). Loops forever: Event_pend(g_midi_uart_event, 0, 3, forever). Bit 1: drains received bytes into 0xC14F11F8 (0xC1620654) and calls MIDIStreamUART::parse. Bit 2: calls the output stream delegate (+8) slot 0 (transmit done). So DIN MIDI input is parsed on its own SYS/BIOS task, not in the UART interrupt.

symbols.name: MIDI::MIDIStreamUART::parse
symbols.prototype: void parse(MIDIStreamUART *this, const uint8_t *bytes /*B4*/, int count /*A6*/)
evidence: Byte-stream MIDI parser with running status (status at this+36, data count at +40, expected length at +44). Real-time bytes (0xF8-0xFF) go to the input stream delegate slot 3 immediately. Complete channel messages go first to the raw consumer at +12 (MIDIStream write with mode 0, used for THRU) and then to the delegate slot 0 (MIDIInputPort::handle_channel_message).

SysEx: 0xF0 starts it (raw consumer mode 1), data bytes go to the raw consumer with mode 2 and are appended to g_midi_sysex_buffer (limit 1024 at +44), 0xF7 goes to the raw consumer with mode 3. The buffer is delivered through delegate slot 2 (MIDIInputPort -> MIDIInputPortDelegate slot 7) as (port, stream, flag A6, buffer B6, length A8): flag 0 = whole message (buffer starts with 0xF0 and ends with 0xF7), 1 = first 1024-byte chunk, 2 = middle chunk, 3 = last chunk.

symbols.name: MIDI::MIDIStreamUART::on_uart_rx
evidence: UARTDriverDelegate slot 1 (thunk 0xC16206D4). Event_post(g_midi_uart_event, 1): wakes task_loop to read and parse.

symbols.name: MIDI::MIDIStreamUART::on_uart_tx_done
evidence: UARTDriverDelegate slot 0 (thunk 0xC16206EC). Event_post(g_midi_uart_event, 2).

Renamed 2026-11-14 from Event_post: simulated, it loads the first word of the wrapper object (the SYS/BIOS Event handle) and branches to 0xC167E600, the exact SYS/BIOS Event_post (claim LIB-3), with the event bits unchanged in B4. The same shape as mailbox_post.

symbols.name: usb_midi_set_delegate

symbols.name: usb_midi_rx_callback

On event 2 (data received) it clears g_usb_midi_rx_buffer (2048 bytes), reads into it via 0xC167D810, then calls g_usb_midi_delegate slot 0 (MIDIStreamUSB::receive) with (delegate, 0, buffer, count). Other events go to 0xC164AD88.

Context (2026-11-10): called only by usb_midi_endpoint_handler's task path (context 0, 0xC162DF24), which usb_task_dispatch reaches from usb_task_loop. The USB interrupt only fills the usblib ring buffer and posts to the USB task. So this callback, MIDIStreamUSB::receive and MainDelegate's MIDI handlers for USB input run in the USB task (priority 14 in SmplTrek, 13 in Lofi-12 XT and CyDrums), not in an interrupt. Correction: the earlier note that 0xC162DD44 calls this callback was wrong; 0xC162DD44 calls dev+12 (the buffer callback) on the interrupt path.

symbols.name: midi_input_from_usb

symbols.name: g_midi_settings
evidence: Words in the settings block at 0xC14Fxxxx (zero-filled at load, filled from saved settings), each with a one-instruction getter/setter pair in 0xC1595000-0xC15957C0. Address corrected 2026-11-09: the MVKH high half is 0xC14F, not 0xC150 as first recorded.

MIDI > CONFIG map, confirmed statically: the page's per-item value functions (0xC15B81E4-0xC15B8AA8) appear in memory in exactly the reverse of its label order (constructor at 0xC15B8E00: INPUT FROM, OUTPUT TO, TX NOTE, TX CC, CLOCK OUT, OUT/THRU, COMMAND, PROGRAM CHANGE, ACTIVE SENS, TX SCENE CHANGE), and every word also gates the matching sender:

[0] 0xC14FAD30 INPUT FROM (1 DIN, 2 USB, 3 both); [1] AD34 OUTPUT TO (same encoding); [2] AD38 PROGRAM CHANGE (2/3 = TX, midi_tx_pc_enabled -> midi_send_program_change); [3] AD3C TX NOTE (!= 0, midi_tx_note_enabled -> note on/off, packed3); [4] AD40 TX CC (!= 0, midi_tx_cc_enabled -> midi_send_cc); [5] AD44 CLOCK OUT (!= 0, midi_clock_out_enabled -> midi_send_clock 0xF8); [6] AD48 OUT/THRU (!= 0 = THRU); [7] AD4C COMMAND (bit 0 RX, bit 1 TX: midi_rx_command_enabled 1/3, midi_tx_command_enabled 2/3 -> start/continue/stop FA/FB/FC); [8] AD50 ACTIVE SENS (2/3 = TX -> 0xFE); TX SCENE CHANGE is the word at 0xC14FAD70 (getter 0xC1595160).
The manual's labels differ slightly: TX PC for PROGRAM CHANGE, and it has no TX SCENE CHANGE row (added after the r2 manual).

Cross-product (2026-11-10): Lofi-12 XT 1.5.205 and CyDrums 1.1.84 keep words [0], [1] and [3]-[8] in this order with the same encodings (their hand symbol files; rows tied to words through each MIDI CONFIG constructor). Their word [2] has no reference and PROGRAM CHANGE is at +0x3C; Lofi-12 XT adds SPP at +0xB0; neither has TX SCENE CHANGE. The array sits at g_settings+0xD8 here and +0xDC in the other two.

evidence: Mode = self+128 (word 32). Mode < 128: returns the mode (fixed velocity). Otherwise returns pad_velocity_from_curve(max(raw, prev_raw), mode - 128).
Matches the manual's PAD VELOCITY setting: 1-127 = 'Velocity is always at this fixed value', then SOFT / LINEAR / HARD (System settings, Pad sensitivity).

evidence: Table = g_pad_velocity_curves + 512*curve (128 words). Counts the leading entries <= peak, searching in four blocks of 32 (it compares against entries 31 and 95 first to pick the block). symbols.name: g_pad_velocity_curves
evidence: Velocity thresholds (raw ADC units) read by pad_velocity_from_curve; three ascending tables from 800 to about 3220 (the next 512 bytes are text, so there are 3).

Curve 0 rises slowly at first (800, 808, 816 ...; entry 60 = 1578), curve 1 is even (800, 819, 838 ...; entry 60 = 1944), curve 2 rises fast (800, 833, 866 ...; entry 60 = 2384). For a given hit curve 0 gives the highest velocity, so 0/1/2 = SOFT/LINEAR/HARD in the manual's order (inferred from shape).

symbols.name: pad_sensor_set_velocity_mode

symbols.name: setting_pad_velocity

symbols.name: setting_set_pad_velocity
evidence: Stores value at 0xC14FACAC (g_setting_pad_velocity). Called only by settings_apply_pad_velocity.

symbols.name: g_setting_pad_velocity
evidence: SYSTEM MENU > PAD VELOCITY. Zero-initialised at load (filled from saved settings). Encoding as read by pad_velocity: 1-127 fixed velocity, 128 + n = curve n (0 SOFT, 1 LINEAR, 2 HARD, order inferred).

symbols.name: settings_apply_pad_velocity

symbols.name: g_pad_sensor
evidence: Passed as self to pad_sensor_update by MainDelegate::on_pad_analog. Layout from pad_sensor_update and helpers: +0 int state[15] (0 idle, 1 down); +60 int release_count[15]; +124 KeyPadDelegate *delegate; +128 int velocity_mode; +132 PadHoldTracker hold {+0 state, +4 pad (-1 none), +8 byte hard, +12 count}.

The delegate word at +124 (0xC1500560) has three writers: start-up clears it (0xC1549B6E), MainDelegate's setup stores MainDelegate+40, its KeyPadDelegate base (0xC154AA90), and AppTestMIDI points it at itself (this+16, 0xC1660D38) and clears it again (0xC1660D4A). So every pad event goes through this one word: a single-word hook for all pads, simpler than patching a vtable.

symbols.name: g_pad_event
evidence: Static message filled by pad_sensor_update before calling delegate slot 0: +0 kind (1 pressed, 0 released), +4 pad, +8 velocity (0 on release). This is the message controllers receive in slot 8.

symbols.name: g_pad_first_raw
evidence: B14+1104. The first raw sample >= 800 from an idle pad; pad_sensor_update uses it as prev_raw for pad_velocity on the next such sample.

symbols.name: g_pad_first_count
evidence: B14+1108. 0 or 1: whether g_pad_first_raw holds a sample. Set to 1 on the first sample, back to 0 after the press is reported.

symbols.name: pad_hold_update
symbols.prototype: int pad_hold_update(PadHoldTracker *t, int pad, int raw)
evidence: Returns 0 unless t tracks this pad (t->pad == pad, t->state != 0). Hard flag (t+8) with hysteresis: set when raw > 2800, cleared when raw < 2400. State 1: becomes 2 once hard. States 2 and 3: while hard, t->count++; in state 2 count reaching 60 sets state 3, count 0 and returns 1; in state 3 count reaching 180 resets the tracker (pad_hold_reset) and returns 2. While not hard, count decays by 1 towards 0.

Effect: pressing one pad hard for 60 samples fires delegate slot 1 once, holding hard for 180 more fires slot 2. Sample rate (and so the time) unknown; the samples come from the panel controller via ADControllerUART.

symbols.name: pad_hold_start
evidence: t->pad = pad, t->state = 1, hard flag = 0, count = 0. Called on every press, so the tracker follows the most recently pressed pad.

symbols.name: pad_hold_reset
evidence: t->state = 0, t->pad = -1, hard flag = 0, count = 0.

symbols.name: pad_hold_current_pad
evidence: Returns t->pad (t+4).

symbols.name: pad_hold_is_armed
evidence: Returns (t->state & ~1) != 0, i.e. state 2 or 3.

symbols.name: pad_sensor_hold_progress
evidence: On the tracker at self+132: returns its count if state == 3, it tracks this pad and the pad is >= 0; otherwise -1. So it reports progress towards the 180-sample long hold. Called (as a tail branch) from 0xC1520D80 with g_pad_sensor and the pad index at B14+1304, in code reached from HomeModeController's pad handlers.

symbols.name: g_control_switch_state
evidence: Zero-initialised; read at about 90 sites; written only by control_switch_poll through g_control_switch_scanner+64 (this word is that field). AppTestControl::draw reads it as one 64-bit word and fills each button of its panel diagram whose bit is set, so it holds the switches currently held down.

symbols.name: audio_block_isr
evidence: Registered by the audio init at 0xC1621884 through 0xC168AB20(0, audio_block_isr, 0), next to the PSC enable of McASP0 (0xC1686A40(0x01E27000, 7, ...)) and the EDMA channel requests for events 0 and 1 (McASP0 receive / transmit on the C6748): a transfer-completion callback for TCC 0, i.e. once per received block.
Each call: Swi_post(g_audio_swi). It also counts calls in B14+908 and every 375th call runs 0xC1660ED4 first; 375 blocks x 128 frames = 48000 frames, so that is a once-per-second tick at 48 kHz.

symbols.name: audio_block_process
evidence: The function of g_audio_swi (compared against it by 0xC16215D8 via Swi_getAttrs), so it runs as a SYS/BIOS Swi once per block.

Picks the receive buffer from the link field of EDMA PaRAM set 0 (0x01C04014 low half == 0x4820 -> 0x11F00C00, else 0x11F00800) and stores it in 0xC16EEBC0; zeroes the float output block (g_audio_out_block +16 left[128], +528 right[128]); calls g_audio_render_callback(&g_audio_out_block) if set; then picks the transmit buffer from PaRAM set 1's link (0x01C04034 == 0x4860 -> 0x11F00400, else 0x11F00000) and writes 128 frames as interleaved int32 = (int)(sample * 2^31) (MPYSP by 0x4F000000, SPTRUNC).
Buffers are 1024 bytes = 128 stereo frames of 32-bit slots, ping-ponged in L1D SRAM (0x11F00000-0x11F00FFF). Samples are floats in [-1, 1).

symbols.name: audio_block_process_monitor
evidence: Same as audio_block_process, but copies the received block into the transmit buffer (0xC16A46A0(tx, rx, 1024), memcpy-like) and adds the rendered samples (int32 add after the 2^31 scaling) instead of overwriting: input passed straight through to the output plus the rendered audio. 0xC16215D8 switches g_audio_swi between the two with Swi_setAttrs.

symbols.name: audio_set_render_callback
evidence: Stores cb in g_audio_render_callback (B14+904). Called with 0xC159AC24 (audio_render_main) from 0xC16520A0 and 0xC16630A0, with 0 (disable) from 0xC1652090 and 0xC1662F60, and with its caller's argument from 0xC16787D0 (which then runs 0xC16215D8, the switch to audio_block_process_monitor).

symbols.name: g_audio_render_callback
evidence: B14+904. Called by audio_block_process(_monitor) once per 128-frame block with &g_audio_out_block; null = silence (the block is zeroed before the call).

symbols.name: g_audio_out_block
evidence: Passed to g_audio_render_callback. +16 float left[128] (0xC16DEB70), +528 float right[128] (0xC16DED70); zeroed before the callback and converted to int32 for the DAC after it. The first 16 bytes are not read here.

Header (copy-table initialised data, read 2026-11-10): {2, 128, 0, 0} = channels, frames per block. Lofi-12 XT and CyDrums use the same layout with 96 frames (R at +16+4*frames there = +400), so code that reads word 1 and puts R at +16+4*frames works on all three.

symbols.name: g_audio_swi
evidence: B14+1464. Posted by audio_block_isr each block; its function is audio_block_process or audio_block_process_monitor.

symbols.name: mcasp_configure
evidence: Calls, all with baseAddr = 0x01D00000 (McASP0), in this order: McASPRxReset, McASPTxReset; McASPRxFmtI2SSet / McASPTxFmtI2SSet(32, 32, 0) (32-bit words in 32-bit slots, DMA port); McASPRxFrameSyncCfg / McASPTxFrameSyncCfg(2, 0x10, 0) (2-slot TDM = I2S, word-wide frame sync, external sync on the rising edge); McASPRxClkCfg(0, 0, 0) (external bit and high-frequency clocks), McASPRxClkPolaritySet(0) (MCASP_RX_CLK_POL_FALL_EDGE), McASPRxClkCheckConfig(5, 0, 255); McASPTxClkCfg(0, 0, 0), McASPTxClkPolaritySet(0x80) (MCASP_TX_CLK_POL_FALL_EDGE), McASPTxClkCheckConfig(5, 0, 255); McASPTxRxClkSyncEnable; McASPRxTimeSlotSet / McASPTxTimeSlotSet(3) (slots 0 and 1); McASPSerializerRxSet(14), McASPSerializerTxSet(13); McASPPinMcASPSet(0xFFFFFFFF); McASPPinDirOutputSet(0x2000) (AXR13); McASPPinDirInputSet(0xB0004000) (AFSR, ACLKR, AFSX, AXR14); McASPTxIntEnable(15), and it tail-calls McASPRxIntEnable(15) (underrun/overrun, sync error, clock fail, DMA error).

Follows McASPI2SConfigure from the StarterWare lcdkC6748 mcasp example (examples/lcdkC6748/mcasp/mcaspPlayBk.c) call for call, with the same serializers (AXR14 in, AXR13 out). Differences from the example: no McASPReadFifoEnable / McASPWriteFifoEnable (the AFIFO is left off); 32-bit words and slots instead of 16; receive frame sync on the rising edge (example: falling) and receive clock polarity MCASP_RX_CLK_POL_FALL_EDGE (example: rising); ACLKX is not in the input pin mask (it is an input anyway after reset). With external bit clocks and frame syncs, the codec is the I2S clock master.

symbols.name: g_flash_memory_driver
evidence: Constructed at 0xC167C6A8 by HAL::FlashMemoryDriver::FlashMemoryDriver(this, &g_spi_driver, 0) during start-up; the app's flash users (0xC159B6xx-0xC159D0xx, next to the FlashDelagate object built at 0xC159B5C4) all pass this object.

Layout as used: +12 HAL::SPIDriver *spi, +16 FlashMemoryDriverDelegate *delegate, +20 semaphore-like object used for blocking waits, +24 event (transfer done), +32 chip select / device argument passed to the SPI driver (0), +36 byte 'synchronous request in flight'.

symbols.name: g_spi_driver
evidence: Its vptr is set to HAL::SPIDriver's vtable (0xC16CF788) at 0xC167C640 and it is passed to the FlashMemoryDriver constructor. Vtable slots used by the flash driver: 0 = select (spi, device, 1 assert / 0 release), 1 = write (spi, bytes, len, flag), 2 = read (spi, buf, len, flag), completion signalled through the driver's event.

symbols.name: g_flash_request_mailbox
evidence: Pended by HAL::FlashMemoryDriver::task_loop, posted by request_read/request_program/request_erase. Message (16 bytes): +0 u16 request id (-1 = synchronous), +2 u16 type (1 read, 2 program, 3 erase, 4 quit), +4 address, +8 length, +12 buffer. Correction 2026-11-10: types 2 and 3 had been recorded the other way round; task_loop dispatches 2 to do_program and 3 to do_erase.

symbols.name: HAL::FlashMemoryDriver::FlashMemoryDriver
evidence: Stores the vptrs (primary 0xC16CC1D0, TaskHandler 0xC16CC1E4 at +4), spi at +12 and device at +32, creates the objects at +20 and +24 (0xC16A1B60/0xC16A1BE4, 0xC16A1B70/0xC16A5168) and clears the byte at +36.

symbols.name: HAL::FlashMemoryDriver::request_read
symbols.prototype: int request_read(HAL::FlashMemoryDriver *this, uint32_t addr, void *buf, uint32_t len, int id)
evidence: Posts {id, 1, addr, len, buf} to g_flash_request_mailbox. With id == -1 it is synchronous: sets this+36, posts, then loops waiting (0xC15DF978: pend on this+20 with timeout 1) until the task clears this+36; in that case the delegate's completion slot is not called. With another id it returns at once and completion arrives through the delegate's slot 1 (op code 2).

Read-only: the request ends in do_read, which issues only READ (0x03) after polling the status register. The call blocks, so it must run in a SYS/BIOS task (e.g. a UI handler on the app message loop), never in a Hwi/Swi. This is the entry point the A4 flash dump used (experiments/README.md): request_read(&g_flash_memory_driver, addr, buf, len, -1). Called about 10 times by the app (e.g. 0xC159B718 reads 0x20000 bytes).

symbols.name: HAL::FlashMemoryDriver::request_program
symbols.prototype: int request_program(HAL::FlashMemoryDriver *this, uint32_t addr, const void *buf, uint32_t len, int id)
evidence: Posts a type 2 request {id, 2, addr, len, buf} (sth 2 at message +2, buf from A6 at +12); same synchronous scheme as request_read. task_loop sends type 2 to do_program (0xC15DF2F4) with addr, len, buf and id from the message (packets 0xC15DF6E0-0xC15DF704, decoded with packets.py). Callers pass a buffer: settings_sector_write_verify programs the payload and then the 4-byte tag with it. WRITES THE SPI FLASH: never call from custom code (SAFETY.md).

Correction 2026-11-10: named request_erase (and 0xC15DFA64 request_program) from 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-10; the type codes had been read as 2 erase / 3 program. The dispatch in task_loop shows 2 = program, 3 = erase.

symbols.name: HAL::FlashMemoryDriver::request_erase
symbols.prototype: int request_erase(HAL::FlashMemoryDriver *this, uint32_t addr, uint32_t len, int id)
evidence: Posts a type 3 request {id, 3, addr, len, 0} (no buffer); returns -1 at once if the address is not 4 KiB aligned (extu 20,20). task_loop sends type 3 to do_erase (0xC15DF060, opcodes 0xD8 / 0x52 / 0x20 chosen by alignment and remaining length; packets 0xC15DF714-0xC15DF71C). settings_save calls it with (driver, sector, 4096, -1) once per sector. WRITES THE SPI FLASH: never call from custom code (SAFETY.md).
Correction 2026-11-10: was named request_program until 2026-11-10 (see request_program at 0xC15DF988).

symbols.name: HAL::FlashMemoryDriver::task_loop
evidence: The driver's task (TaskHandler entry via the thunk 0xC15DF860). Mailbox_pend(g_flash_request_mailbox, msg, -1) forever; type 1 -> do_read, 2 -> do_erase (0xC15DF060), 3 -> do_program (0xC15DF2F4), 4 -> return. After each request: if the synchronous flag (+36) is set it is cleared, else delegate->slot1(delegate, this, op, id) with op 2 read, 0 erase, 1 program.

symbols.name: HAL::FlashMemoryDriver::do_read
symbols.prototype: int do_read(HAL::FlashMemoryDriver *this, uint32_t addr, void *buf, uint32_t len, int id)
evidence: wait_ready first (returns -1 if it fails). Command buffer {0x03, addr[23:16], addr[15:8], addr[7:0]} (put_address). Loop: select, write the 4 command bytes, read min(len, 0xFFFF) bytes via SPI slot 2, Event_pend(this+24, ..., 1000) for completion, release; on success advance buf/addr/len and call delegate->slot0 (progress: delegate, this, 2, ...); on error or timeout retry, giving up after 3 failures. Returns 0.
3-byte addressing, so the code can address at most 16 MiB. The flash size itself is not read here (no JEDEC ID 0x9F command found in the driver).

symbols.name: HAL::FlashMemoryDriver::do_program
symbols.prototype: int do_program(HAL::FlashMemoryDriver *this, uint32_t addr, const void *buf, uint32_t len, int id)
evidence: Builds command 0x02 (PAGE PROGRAM) and writes in 256-byte pages with status polling. B6 is tested as the length, so buf is A6 and len B6 (simulated 2026-11-13, analysis/flash_cmd_map.py; this prototype listed len before buf until then). WRITES THE SPI FLASH: never call from custom code (SAFETY.md).

symbols.name: HAL::FlashMemoryDriver::do_erase
symbols.prototype: int do_erase(HAL::FlashMemoryDriver *this, uint32_t addr, uint32_t len, int id)
evidence: Uses the erase commands 0xD8 (64 KiB block), 0x52 (32 KiB block) and 0x20 (4 KiB sector); the selection logic is not read in detail. WRITES THE SPI FLASH: never call from custom code (SAFETY.md).

symbols.name: ADControllerUART::task_loop

symbols.name: ADControllerUART::parse
evidence: Drains received bytes (0xC161BAD8) and runs a byte-level state machine: a byte with bit 7 set starts a packet and its high nibble selects the type (cases 1-8 at 0xC161E040-0xC161E108), data bytes are 7-bit and are shifted together (shl 7) into a 14-bit value; completed analogue values go to the ADControllerDelegate at this+20 slot 1 (channel, value), which is MainDelegate::on_pad_analog for channels 0-14. Details of each packet type not read.

Protocol (read 2026-11-10; the function is identical in Lofi-12 XT and CyDrums apart from data layout): state at this+32. In the idle state every received byte is first passed to the delegate's slot 0 (delegate, this, byte). 0xBn starts an analogue packet for channel n (n = low nibble, kept at B14+1216); the next two bytes are 7-bit, low part first: value = b1 | b2 << 7 (14 bits). The value is stored at this+36+2n and sent to delegate slot 1 (delegate, this, channel, value). 0xA1 starts a 6-byte packet whose 7-bit bytes are stored at this+70..+75 with no callback (meaning not known). Other status bytes are ignored. The delegate pointer is at this+20, so one word (g_ad_controller_uart+20) routes every analogue panel value in every product.

symbols.name: g_control_switch_scanner
evidence: Produces every button event. Layout: +0 bit set being auto-repeated, +4 repeat start time, +8 last repeat time, +12 repeat delay (400 first, then 100), +16 byte repeat armed, +17 byte repeat count flag, +20 hardware source object (vtable; polled by control_switch_poll), +24 ControlSwitchDelegate * (MainDelegate+28, stored by MainDelegate's setup at 0xC154AA68 through 0xC1501DC8), +32 previous raw reading (64-bit), +64 the held-switch word = g_control_switch_state (0xC1501DF0).
Initialised by control_switch_init (via 0xC168B584) and 0xC1653860 (called from 0xC154A590).

symbols.name: control_switch_init
evidence: this+20 = source, this+24 = 0 (delegate set later by MainDelegate), this+64 = 0 (no switches held).

symbols.name: control_switch_poll
evidence: Reads the source through its vtable, merges the field it reports into a 64-bit reading, and if it differs from the held word walks the bits one by one: a newly set bit is ORed into this+64 and reported as {bit, code 1} (pressed), and arms auto-repeat for it (control_switch_repeat_start); a cleared bit is removed from this+64 and reported as {bit, code 0} (released), disarming repeat. Each report is a single-bit ControlSwitchMessage sent to the delegate's slot 0 (MainDelegate::post_control_switch, the queued path). Called from 0xC16766A4.
So g_control_switch_state is written only here (through this+64), which is why no absolute-address store to it exists.

symbols.name: control_switch_repeat_start
evidence: Arms auto-repeat: +0 = the pressed bit(s), +4 = +8 = now, +12 = 400 (first delay), +16 = 1, +17 = 0.

symbols.name: control_switch_repeat_tick
evidence: When now - last > delay (and the armed bit is still held): the first time sends {bits, code 1, second word 1} through delegate slot 1 (empty in MainDelegate) and sets +17; later times send {bits, code 1, second word 2} through delegate slot 2 (MainDelegate::dispatch_control_switch, direct to the controller), counting in B14+1276; the delay then becomes 100. With the 400 / 100 delays this is the usual key auto-repeat; the dispatcher's special case for the four directions and the two octave keys (code 1) is where repeats are honoured.
Message layout seen here: +0 u64 bits, +8 u16 code, +10 u16 (0 normal, 1 first hold, 2 repeat; inferred from the byte stores at sp+12..15).

symbols.name: codec_write
symbols.prototype: int codec_write(uint32_t i2c_base, int reg, int value)
evidence: Writes one codec register over I2C (A4 = I2C0 base 0x01C22000, B4 = register, A6 = value). 86 call sites; the registers written are 0-7, 10, 15-19, 21, 22, 24, 41-44, 47, 51, 58, 65, 82, 85, 86, 92, 93 and 107, which matches the TI TLV320AIC310x (AIC3104/AIC3106) page-0 map: 0 page select, 1 reset, 2 sample rate, 3-6 PLL, 7 datapath, 10 interface, 15/16 ADC PGA gain, 17-24 input routing, 41/42 DAC output switching and pop control, 43/44 DAC digital volume, 47-65 headphone outputs, 82-93 line outputs. With the slave address 0x18 this identifies an AIC310x-family codec (exact part not distinguishable from the map).

symbols.name: audio_clock_probe_tick
evidence: Called once per second of audio (every 375th block) by audio_block_isr. Does nothing unless the byte at B14+560 is set; then it reads the 64-bit timer at 0x01C21000 (via 0xC1660E80 / 0xC165E6E0) and stores the difference from the previous second into a 10-entry table at 0xC1503480 (index B14+568). A measurement of the audio clock against the CPU timer, presumably for a test page; name reflects the behaviour.

symbols.name: g_settings_ext
evidence: Filled by settings_validate from the PREX block or with defaults; followed at +372 (0xC14F9860) by its shadow copy.

Layout (2026-11-10): +0 'PREX' tag; +4 USB AUDIO track settings and +56 EXT SRC track settings, the same layout (word fields +0..+36, each with a getter and setter: 0xC164C8D8-0xC164CE20 for +4, 0xC1619B68-0xC161A36C for +56); +108 a smaller block (byte +0, words +4 / +8; inference: the EXT SRC audio-file selection); +364 a word that only the defaults, change check and validator touch. Which block is which: the per-track parameter dispatcher at 0xC154D0E0 maps track type 7 to the +4 setters and type 8 to the +56 setters, and the type table 0xC16ED768 gives type 6 to tracks 10-12 (the three GLOBAL tracks), 7 to track 13 and 8 to track 14, matching the manual's order (10 sequencer tracks, 3 GLOBAL, USB AUDIO, EXT SRC); the +4 accessors' other callers sit next to AppUSBTrackSetting's methods (0xC1638E38) and the +56 ones next to AppEXTTrackSetting's (0xC1592960). Per-field labels not mapped. Lofi-12 XT / CyDrums reset their PREX to defaults on every boot (platform map 'Settings block').

2026-11-15: the two track blocks are 52 bytes each; +0 LEVEL, +4 PAN, +16 SEND, +20 EQ TYPE, +24 EQ FREQ, +28 EQ AMOUNT, +36 HOLD/GATE, bytes +40..+42 TRACK COLOR levels and +43 its index, byte +48 MUTE; +8, +12, +32 and bytes +44..+47, +49, +50 unlabelled. Simulated through the track_set_* dispatchers (01-platform-map.md 'PREF fields', PREX). Corrects 'word fields +0..+36' above.

symbols.name: g_settings
evidence: Filled by settings_validate from the PREF block or with defaults; followed at +284 (0xC14FAD74) by its shadow copy.

symbols.name: settings_changed
evidence: Compares g_settings with its shadow 0xC14FAD74 byte by byte (284), then g_settings_ext with its shadow 0xC14F9860 (372); returns 1 if any byte differs, else 0. Called first thing by settings_save, which writes nothing when it returns 0.

Correction 2026-11-10: was named settings_block_build ("fills the 4 KiB write image"); the write image is filled per half by the callbacks settings_pref_fill / settings_prex_fill that settings_save passes to settings_sector_write_verify.

symbols.name: settings_validate
evidence: Compares block[0..3] with g_settings_tag ('PREF'): match -> memcpy(&g_settings, block, 284); mismatch -> fills g_settings with defaults (tempo 100 etc.) and returns -1. Then compares block[0xC00..0xC03] with g_settings_ext_tag ('PREX'): match -> memcpy(&g_settings_ext, block + 0xC00, 372); mismatch -> defaults and -1.

Afterwards range-clamps every field it knows (helpers 0xC15956E4, 0xC15958B0, 0xC15958D8, 0xC15958F8, 0xC1595918, 0xC1595934, 0xC1595950, 0xC1595784, 0xC1595828; byte arrays clamped in sploops), then copies both structs to the shadow copies immediately after them (284 and 372 bytes). Only the tags are validated: no CRC, no length, no version field.

Lofi-12 XT 1.5.205 (validator 0xC2BD31AC, main payload 404 bytes) and CyDrums 1.1.84 use the same two tags, so a block written by another product passes this check. Relevant to any cross-flash (session C3).

symbols.name: settings_sector_write_verify
evidence: Writes one tagged half-sector (called four times by settings_save, after the sector erase): memset(0xC14C0400, 0, 8192); len = fill(0xC14C0400) (284 or 372, tag word included); Cache_wbInv(buf, 8192) through the wrapper 0xC16A1B38; request_program(addr + 4, buf + 4, len - 4); request_read(addr, buf + 4096, len) and compare bytes 4..len-1 with the source; only if they match, request_program(addr, buf, 4) writes the 4-byte tag last. No retry loop. The rest of the half (up to 0xC00 or 0x1000) is left erased (0xFF).

Correction 2026-11-10: earlier described as erase, re-read and retry up to 4 times with a buffer argument (the 4 compared with A13 is the tag-only length). Lofi-12 XT equivalent 0xC2C8AFA8, CyDrums 0xC24C4300 (16 KiB buffer).

symbols.name: settings_save
evidence: Calls settings_changed (0xC1594BEC) and returns without writing if it returns 0. Otherwise, for sector 0x01FFF000 and then 0x01FFE000: request_erase(driver, sector, 4096, -1), then settings_sector_write_verify(sector, settings_pref_fill) for the PREF half at +0 and settings_sector_write_verify(sector + 0xC00, settings_prex_fill) for the PREX half. Addresses built with SET a4,12,24 / 10,24 / 13,24 and mvk -5120 + mvkh 0x01FF0000: 0x01FFF000, 0x01FFFC00, 0x01FFE000, 0x01FFEC00. (Corrected 2026-11-10: earlier recorded as request_program with a buffer and an erase-and-verify helper.)

The only path to request_erase / request_program in the app (4 call sites, all here and in settings_sector_write_verify). Two entries (correction 2026-11-10: earlier recorded as a single caller): the direct call at 0xC154AE60 inside 0xC1549F6C, and settings_reset_and_save (0xC159CEA4), which tail-calls it. Identical code in Lofi-12 XT at 0xC2C8B0F8 and in CyDrums at 0xC24C4458.

Return value: if settings_block_build returns 0 nothing is written; either way the function ends by polling the flash status register (read_status, sleeping one tick per busy poll) and returns with A4 = the last status value (WIP clear). No caller uses it: at 0xC154AE64 the next instruction calls tick_count, which overwrites A4, and the caller only waits until 1000 ticks (1 s) have passed since it started; the wrapper's callers discard it too. Lofi-12 XT (0xC2BAD7BC) and CyDrums (0xC24CE9D8) have the same caller code. So a patched entry `b b3; nop 5` cannot cause a retry; `mvk 0, a4` in front is still harmless.

symbols.name: settings_load
evidence: Reads 4096 bytes from flash 0x01FFF000 (device 1, 0xFFF000) into g_settings_read_buf with request_read(..., -1) and calls settings_validate(buf, 4096); if that returns negative, reads 0x01FFE000 and validates again, returning the second result. Called once from the app init function 0xC1549F6C, which ignores the result.

symbols.name: HAL::FlashMemoryDriver::select_device
evidence: Compares device with this+32 (set by the constructor); if different calls 0xC1626D28 with this+28 and the new device, then stores it at this+32. Only caller: flash_select_address.

symbols.name: flash_select_address
evidence: Whole body: if addr < 0x01000000 call FlashMemoryDriver::select_device(&g_flash_memory_driver, 0) and return addr; else select_device(..., 1) and return addr - 0x01000000. Every app flash read/erase/program passes its address through this first (settings reader 0xC159CEB4, writer 0xC159CD84, erase-and-verify 0xC159CC34).
So the app addresses two 16 MiB SPI flash devices as one 32 MiB space; device 1 holds the top half. This closes the question of how 0x01FFxxxx fits 24-bit addressing.

evidence: step = (target - *state) * 0.0078125 (0x3C000000 = 1/128), *state = target, then multiplies L (+16) and R (+528) of the block by a gain moving linearly from the old state towards target, frame count from block+4, unrolled by 4 (constants 3.0, 4.0). A per-block de-zippered gain.

This is the only path by which the input reaches the output, apart from the setting-25 loop-back in 0xC159A9F8.

symbols.name: audio_mix_main
evidence: Called from audio_render_main with (out, 0) after the input processing. Calls other render engines (0xC1645xxx, 0xC15AAxxx, 0xC1625xxx) and virtual methods on objects from tables 0xC14C4220 / 0xC14C2404, sums them into out, and ends with audio_gain_ramp(state B14+1128). The sources are identified in the next item.

Effect stage (2026-11-10): after the sources, the selected g_send_effects member (delay/reverb, or SideChainCompressor via vtbl[+12]) is called with (0xC16DFFB0 block, 0xC16DE750 block) and the 0xC16DE750 block is added into out; then the selected g_master_effects member is called with (0xC16DFFB0 block, out); then audio_gain_ramp(B14+1128, 0xC158A520(), out). The source engines before that (0xC1645508/0xC15AA344/0xC1645304, 0xC15AAFE8/0xC15AABD4, 0xC1625BF8/0xC1625D8C, 0xC15AAAD0) are still unidentified.

Track sources (2026-11-10): with second argument != 1 (audio_render_main passes 0) it calls 0xC15AAFE8(0xC16E07D0 block, 0xC16DFFB0 block), which calls TrackSound::USBTrack::render on g_usb_track, and then 0xC15AABD4, which calls TrackSound::ExtTrack::render on g_ext_track; with 1 it skips both ([a0] bnop at 0xC159A1B6). Both continue with loops making virtual calls through vtable +12 (the track render slot) and end with [B14+1016]->vtbl[+12] or 0xC15AA1EC. Bit permutation (2026-11-10, by evaluating the execute packets 0xC166D898-0xC166D920, return delay slots included, one input bit at a time): bit 0 GP3[14], 1 GP3[15], 2 GP3[12], 3 GP3[10], 4 GP5[2], 5 GP5[0], 6 GP5[5], 7 GP5[4], 8 GP5[7], 9 GP5[8]; so encoder 0 = GP3[14]/GP3[15], 1 = GP3[12]/GP3[10], 2 = GP5[2]/GP5[0], 3 = GP5[5]/GP5[4], 4 = GP5[7]/GP5[8] (phase bit 0 / bit 1). Which physical knob has which index is not checked.
Identical in Lofi-12 XT 1.5.205 (0xC2C8FF00) and CyDrums 1.1.84 (0xC259BAE0): region_diff, 0 differences.

symbols.name: encoder_update
evidence: Quadrature decoder for one encoder (24-byte object): +0 encoder index, +4 RotaryEncoderDelegate *, +8 last phase, +12 direction state, +16 accumulated steps, +20 call counter. Returns early (only counting) when the phase is unchanged. Phase 3 is the rest position: it clears the direction state; the first change after it sets the direction (phase 1 -> state 2, phase 2 -> state 1); each later arrival at phase 0 adds -1 (state 2) or +1 (state 1) to the accumulator, and other changes add nothing, so one step per clean detent (3-1-0-2-3 is -1). Simulated 2026-11-13 (analysis/input_map.py); an earlier reading here said every later change adds a step.

Every call increments +20; at 16 it calls delegate slot 0 (delegate, enc, index, steps) if a delegate is set and steps != 0, then clears +16 and +20. Slot 0 of MainDelegate's RotaryEncoderDelegate is post_encoder_event. No time input and no acceleration.

Lofi-12 XT and CyDrums keep this algorithm as the virtual RotaryEncoder::update (vtable slot 0), but they never construct a RotaryEncoder; they run RotaryEncoderV2 instead (see their hand symbol files). region_diff --at against Lofi 0xC2C8FFE8: 82 vs 82 instructions, and every difference is a field offset (a vptr at +0; accumulator at +24) or a branch offset.

symbols.name: encoders_init

So the loop runs 5 times (SPLOOPD: ILC + 4/ii iterations) and encoder i gets index i.

Its address is the tick function stored in the timer object whose period word is at 0xC16ECF18 (decompressed copy-table data).

symbols.name: g_clock_timer_period
evidence: Word 1000 (0x3E8) in initialised data (decoded from the copy table with memory_map.build_map), followed by 0 (periodType, read as microseconds), interrupt number 14 and the tick function clock_tick: the timer that drives the SYS/BIOS Clock. So one Clock tick = 1000 us = 1 ms. Field layout read against SYS/BIOS's timer object as an inference; the same words appear in all three products. A 24000000 (24 MHz timer input) table is nearby in the same data.

symbols.name: task_handler_set
evidence: Two cases, chosen by the sign of B4. Negative (a pointer, 0x8.......+): th+4 = arg and 0xC16ACF80(arg, th) stores th at arg+44 (binds a SYS/BIOS task object to the handler; inference). Otherwise, if th+4 is set: 0xC166F540(th+4 value, arg): sets the bound task's priority to arg (inference: 0xC166F540 locks the scheduler through the Task module state like SYS/BIOS Task_setPri).

All eight priority calls in SmplTrek 3.2.174 (2026-11-10): HAL::FlashMemoryDriver 14 (0xC15DFC4C), AudioFileControlTask 1 (audio_file_control_task_start), ADControllerUART 13 (0xC161E490), MIDI::MIDIStreamUART 13 (0xC1620ED8), GraphicsTaskHandler 15 (graphics_task_set_priority), IOObserver 13 (io_observer_set_priority), AsyncTaskHandler 7 (async_task_handler_start), USBTaskHandler 14 (usb_task_start). Correction: the earlier '15/3' was one call with 15; the MVK 3 belongs to the next function. Byte-identical in Lofi-12 XT (0xC2CCB838) and CyDrums (0xC25E27B8) (func_match hash).
Every task starts at priority -1 (inactive) in the static Task table (g_task_objects), so task_handler_set with a priority is what starts a task. The pointer case is task_handler_bind (0xC168EED0).

symbols.name: ADControllerUART::set_task_priority
evidence: Whole body: tail call task_handler_set(this + 4, 13) (five delay slots: add, mvk 13, nop 3). Called once, from MainDelegate's setup (0xC154A8A0) with g_ad_controller_uart, just before the 460800-baud set-up.

This is the 'fixed 13' panel difference. Lofi-12 XT (0xC2C5C7F0) and CyDrums (0xC25775D0) have the same tail call but leave B4 as received. Correction 2026-11-10: their caller (MainDelegate setup) does load B4: MVK 12 sits in the same execute packet as the call (0xC2BACE24 / 0xC24CE26C, p-bits decoded), so their panel task runs at 12. SmplTrek's caller passes nothing and the callee fixes 13 (the compiler folded the constant, inference). The same holds for the IOObserver task (io_observer_set_priority). Earlier correction: the platform map first placed this at 0xC161E48C as a tail call of the preceding function; 0xC161E48C is that function's last packet and 0xC161E490 starts this one.

symbols.name: settings_reset_and_save
evidence: Whole body: calls settings_set_defaults (0xC1594CAC), then tail-calls settings_save (B to 0xC159CD84 with B3 restored in the delay slots). So settings_save has two entries: this wrapper and the direct call at 0xC154AE60.

Callers 0xC1654884 and 0xC1676124, next to the code that references the 'SYSTEM RESET' (0xC165453C) and 'ALL SYSTEM SETTINGS' (0xC1676168) strings. Both call 0xC158CD68 next, whose first callee 0xC1595588 loads A4 from memory before reading it, so the returned value is discarded. Same wrapper in Lofi-12 XT (0xC2C8B204, caller 0xC2CACD64) and CyDrums (0xC24C4564, caller 0xC25C8264).

symbols.name: settings_set_defaults
evidence: Starts by storing the 'PREF' tag word (g_settings_tag, 0xC16D45E8) into g_settings+0 (0xC14FAC58) and constants into the following fields; only the first packets were read. Called by settings_reset_and_save (reached from next to the SYSTEM RESET / ALL SYSTEM SETTINGS strings), so it most likely resets the settings to defaults before the save.

symbols.name: flash_headers_request
evidence: Sets bits 0-2 (|= 7) in g_flash_delegate+4 (0xC1505214, the pending mask), then posts three asynchronous 128-byte reads with request_read(&g_flash_memory_driver, flash_select_address(addr), buf, 128, id): id 1 from 0x0003FFE4 into g_boot_header, id 4 from 0x00040000 into g_system_header, id 2 from 0x00440000 into g_preset_header. Addresses, buffers and the length come from one-instruction getters (0xC164C328 = 0x3FFE4, 0xC164C320 = 0x40000 via SET a4,18,18, 0xC164C120 = MVKH 0x440000; 0xC164C76C / 0xC164C74C / 0xC164C34C buffers; 0xC164C734 / 0xC164C5A0 / 0xC164C334 return 128 per the objdump decode of the compact MVK, consistent with the 0x80 spacing of the buffers). Ghidra's listing omits the compact instructions in these getters.

These are the app's only reads outside the settings sectors in 0xC159CF..: device 0 holds 'bmtd' (boot) ending at 0x40000, the 'mmtd' system image header at 0x40000 and the 'pmtd' content header at 0x440000 (the content partitions start at 0x441000). Completion arrives in FlashDelagate::on_read_done. Lofi-12 XT (0xC2C8B2D0) and CyDrums (0xC24C54D8) read only the boot and system headers, with ids 1 and 2.

symbols.name: FlashDelagate::on_read_done
evidence: FlashDelagate vtable 0xC16D06B8 slot 1 (HAL::FlashMemoryDriverDelegate; the class name is spelled this way in the RTTI). Request id in B6: 1 -> g_boot_header, 2 -> g_preset_header, 4 -> g_system_header; invalidates the cache over the 128-byte buffer (0xC16A1B20) and clears the id's bit in this+4 (ANDN). Branch structure read; other arguments not decoded.

symbols.name: g_flash_delegate

symbols.name: g_boot_header

symbols.name: g_system_header

symbols.name: g_preset_header

symbols.name: boot_version_string
evidence: Compares g_boot_header[0..3] with 'bmtd' (0xC16CE200). On a match it loads the word at g_boot_header+12 and tests bit 0: set gives '*.*.*' (0xC16CE1F5), clear gives version_words_format(g_boot_header+16, static buffer 0xC16EE3D0), i.e. the version triplet at +16/+20/+24. No match also gives '*.*.*'. Called by the SYSTEM INFO page for the BOOT row (0xC1666E80). Correction 2026-11-11: this was recorded as formatting the word at +12; +12 is a flag word (0xFFFFFFFE in all three headers of the A4 dump, 0xFFFFFFFF in update-file image headers).

symbols.name: system_version_string

symbols.name: preset_version_string

symbols.name: operator_new
evidence: Unique 128-byte relocation-masked match to _Znwj in TI CGT 8.3.13 rts6740_elf.lib new.cpp.obj (work/libmatch-8.3.13.json); checked against the locally installed libcxx/new.cpp and the full listing.

Maps zero size to 1, calls bios_malloc at 0xC169C6C0, and on NULL consults the new-handler pointer at 0xC150174C. Calls a non-NULL handler and retries; returns NULL if no handler is installed. Handler state at runtime is not observed. Decoded startup data initializes the handler to zero.
Stock example: audio_file_stream_create at 0xC15B03D4 requests 108 bytes, then constructs AudioEngine::AudioFileStream at 0xC15AFE80. See docs/07-ram-allocation.md.

symbols.name: bios_malloc
evidence: Whole wrapper 0xC169C6C0..0xC169C72F: zero size returns NULL. For nonzero size, initializes a 32-byte local error block via 0xC16A4DA0, then calls Memory_alloc(NULL, size + 8, 0, &error_block). Ghidra listing and objdump agree on the call argument packet at 0xC169C6E4.

On success, raw[0] = raw and raw[1] = size + 8; returned pointer = raw + 8. Local failure path returns NULL. The size+8 addition has no overflow guard. Configured error policy is return/unwind with a non-NULL local block, but logging/output backend behavior is not yet established; see docs/07-ram-allocation.md.

symbols.name: bios_memalign
evidence: Prologue read 0xC1694760..0xC16947D0: returns NULL (branch to 0xC16947E0) when size is 0 or align is not a power of two; align below 8 becomes 8; then Memory_alloc(NULL, size + align, align, &local error block) and, on success, a header for bios_free in front of the returned pointer (same scheme as bios_malloc: raw pointer and size words at p-8 / p-4). The tail after 0xC16947D0 was not read.

18 call sites. file_open calls it with (128, 556) for the FIL and file_close frees that FIL with bios_free, so bios_free is the release function for this allocator too. Used by the A4 flash-dump probe for its two 128-byte-aligned read buffers (experiments/README.md 'A4 flash dump').

symbols.name: bios_free
evidence: Whole wrapper 0xC16A4820..0xC16A484B, also checked in Ghidra listing: NULL is a no-op; raw = word(ptr - 8), saved = word(ptr - 4); tail-calls Memory_free(NULL, raw, saved + (ptr - raw) - 8). For bios_malloc this frees the original size + 8 allocation.

Do not pass a raw Memory_alloc result to this wrapper: it expects the private header. C++ delete at 0xC16AC600 forwards here; sized-delete thunk 0xC16AC620 forwards to that delete. AudioFileStream destroy at 0xC15B0384 reaches sized delete at 0xC15B03C4.

symbols.name: AudioEngine::AudioFileControlTask::run
evidence: AudioFileControlTask vtable slot 0 (RTTI). Loops on mailbox_pend(g_audio_file_control_mailbox 0xC1500694, &msg, -1). The message is five words {cmd, stream, m2, m3, m4} (stack +4..+20); cmd 0 -> 0xC1609A04, 1-2 inline at 0xC160996C, 3-12 through the jump table at 0xC16F2580 (index cmd*4-12), others re-pend. stream is a 72-byte object (afc_stream_init): 8 zeroed bytes, an AudioEngine::ExpandedWavFile at +8 (RTTI vptr 0xC16CE6A8; FIL* at +12, base offset at +32) and the listener at +60; a null stream makes the stream commands no-ops.

Commands, read packet by packet 2026-11-10 (the request functions that build each message are named AudioFileControlTask::post_*): 0 write block: AudioEngine::WavFile::write (vtable slot 0; fs, m4 = buffer, &m3 = length), then afc_stream_notify_written (listener slot 1), Event_post if m2, then card_space_check(0); when it returns 0 (less than 128 MiB free) it posts app message {5, 2, -1, 0} if app_state_is_4(), nothing if app_state_is_2(), else {5, 2, -2, 0} (app_post_message, no wait; handled by MainDelegate::handle_app_message_5). 1 / 2 / 3 read: if AudioEngine::WavFile::tell(fs) != m2, AudioEngine::WavFile::seek(fs, m2); then AudioEngine::WavFile::read (vtable slot 1; fs, m4 = buffer, &m3 = length); 2 also calls afc_stream_notify_read (listener slot 0); 3 posts the event (synchronous read). 4 seek: AudioEngine::WavFile::seek(fs, m2). 5 open: AudioEngine::WavFile::open(fs, m4 = path, (u8)m2 = mode); with m3 (wait) the result goes to the event, without it to afc_stream_notify_opened (listener slot 2). 6: nothing (re-pend; no request function sends it). 7 write and close: if m2 and m4, slot 0 (fs, m4, &m2); AudioEngine::WavFile::close(fs); event if m3. 8 close and free: AudioEngine::WavFile::close(fs), 0xC16AC620(stream, 72) (the sized-delete thunk); event if m2. 9 write and flush: if m3 and m4, slot 0 (fs, m4, &m3); AudioEngine::WavFile::flush(fs); event if m2. 10 file_exists(m4), 11 file_mkdir(m4), 12 file_unlink(m4), all synchronous.

Completion: Event_post(g_audio_file_control_event, 1) for success, or for a nonzero result of file_exists / file_mkdir / file_unlink (so the unlink and mkdir requests return 1 when the FatFs call failed); Event_post(..., -1) otherwise. The requesters wait with Event_pend(event, 0, -1, -1). Corrections to the 2026-11-10 first reading: 3 is tell / seek / read, not 0xC1616648(m1, m2); 5 is open(fs, path, mode), not (m1, m1 != 0, m4 != 0); 7 and 9 write the last buffer before close / flush; 0-2 are now read.

Lofi-12 XT (0xC2C524D8) and CyDrums (0xC2572638) run their own version with commands 0-11 (no no-op 6, so SmplTrek's 7-12 are their 6-11), open always synchronous, and a larger stream object; see their hand files.

Same methods in Lofi-12 XT 1.5.205 (object 0xC2B7E65C) and CyDrums 1.1.84 (0xC242F79C): region_diff 0xC1646AC0-0xC16470B0 with --at 0xC2C7A800 / 0xC2593160, 431 instructions each, only 18 data-page offsets differ (2026-11-10).

symbols.name: g_battery_monitor
evidence: Initialised data: +8 = 4. battery_set_type stores two threshold-table pointers at +0 / +4 (0xC16CE850 + 8 * type and 0xC16CE970 + 8 * type, four halfwords each) and recomputes +8; battery_sample keeps the averaged raw value at +12 (u16) and the level at +8; battery_level_get returns +8 (0-4, inference: 4 = full).

symbols.name: power_gpio_init
evidence: In .init_array (word at 0xC16F3B80). Stores gpio_pin_number(3, 0) at B14+320, gpio_pin_number(4, 11) at B14+324 and gpio_pin_number(3, 7) at B14+328 (each store sits in the execute packet of the next call).

Roles from use (inference): GP3[0] is the power key input (read by power_key_poll and power_on_check, active low), GP4[11] the power-hold output (power_on_check writes 1, power_hold_release writes 0), GP3[7] the power-source input (power_source_read). Same pins in Lofi-12 XT and CyDrums (region_diff keeps the constants).

symbols.name: power_source_read
evidence: Returns 2 when gpio_read(GP3[7], handle at B14+328) is 1, else 1. power_manager_poll stores it at g_power_manager+0 and calls delegate slot 5 when it changes; the battery level is queried only while it is 2 (inference: 2 = running on batteries).

symbols.name: power_hold_release
evidence: Whole body: tail call gpio_write(GP4[11] (B14+324), 0); the argument is not used. Called last by MainDelegate::handle_power_message (0xC154AEA0, after settings_save, the 1 s wait and graphics_task_stop) and by power_on_check when the key is released within about 0.5 s of power-on. Inference: GP4[11] holds the power supply on; clearing it switches the unit off.

symbols.name: power_manager_init
evidence: Stores -1 at +4 and +16 (level unknown, auto power off disabled), 0 at +0, +8, +20, +24 and bytes +28..+32. Called by input_static_init with 0xC15036E8.

symbols.name: power_key_poll
evidence: Nothing until byte +30 (key enabled) is set. Until the key has been seen released (byte +29), reading GP3[0] = 1 sets +29. Afterwards: while the pin reads 1, +8 = tick_count(); while it reads 0 and more than 1000 ticks have passed since +8, it clears +28 and calls the delegate's slot 2 (power-off request). So holding the power key for more than 1 s asks the app to power off. Called from power_manager_poll.

symbols.name: power_auto_off_check
evidence: Returns unless the timeout at +16 is set (not -1). If byte +31 (input activity) is set, or delegate slot 0 returns non-zero (MainDelegate: something is busy), it restarts the idle time (+20 = now, +31 = 0). Otherwise, when now - +20 exceeds +16, it clears +28 and calls delegate slot 2 (power-off request). Called from power_manager_poll.

symbols.name: power_battery_level_set
symbols.prototype: int power_battery_level_set(PowerManager *pm, int level, unsigned now)
evidence: If level equals +4, returns 1. Otherwise stores level at +4 and now at +12, and calls delegate slot 3 (delegate, pm, level); returns 1. Called from power_manager_poll unless byte +32 is set.

symbols.name: power_manager_poll
evidence: Called by IOObserver::run every 32 ticks (when the low five bits of its counter B14+1308 are 16). Returns while byte +28 is clear. Otherwise: level = delegate slot 1 if the source (+0) is 2, else -1; src = power_source_read(); if src differs from +0, stores it and calls delegate slot 5 (delegate, pm, src); then power_key_poll, power_auto_off_check(pm, now), and power_battery_level_set(pm, level, now) unless byte +32 is set.
Read packet by packet. The fetch packet at 0xC1646E80 has the header PROT bit (0x00100000) set, so its back-to-back dependent loads (vptr at 0xC1646E94, slot at 0xC1646E98) execute in order.

symbols.name: power_set_auto_off_timeout
evidence: Stores ms at +16 and tick_count() at +20. Called only by auto_power_off_apply (-1 = off).

symbols.name: power_low_battery_tick
evidence: Called by IOObserver::run once per 1024 ticks (counter value 256). Returns unless the level at +4 is 0 or 1 (unsigned compare); then, when now - +12 exceeds 30000, calls delegate slot 4 (delegate, pm) and stores now at +12. MainDelegate's slot 4 requests a redraw, so with a low battery the display is refreshed every 30 s (inference: a low-battery indication).

symbols.name: power_on_check
evidence: Returns 2 if byte +28 is already set, and 0 at once if the power key (GP3[0]) reads 1 (not held) at entry (simulated 2026-11-13, analysis/input_map.py; an earlier reading here said 2: the 0 is set in a branch delay slot). Otherwise it re-reads the key every 50 ms (task_sleep(50), 10 tries); if the key is still pressed it writes GP4[11] = 1 (power hold), sets +28, stores tick_count() at +20 and returns 1; if it was released, it calls power_hold_release and keeps looping (inference: waits for the power to fail). Called once by MainDelegate start-up (0xC154A8F4).

symbols.name: gpio_pin_number
evidence: Returns bank * 16 + pin + 1 (StarterWare's 1-based GPIO pin number), computed in the delay slots of BNOP B3,2.

symbols.name: gpio_write

symbols.name: task_sleep

symbols.name: battery_sample
evidence: Called by IOObserver::run once per 1024 ticks (counter 1023) with the halfword at 0xC1501A12 = g_ad_controller_uart + 66, i.e. panel analogue channel 15 (pads use 0-14). Lofi-12 XT 0xC2BCE920 and CyDrums 0xC24ED8A0 (called from the same place in IOObserver::run): same constants and structure, scheduled slightly differently (region_diff to 0xC158CA24: 49 other differences, encodings and packing).

symbols.name: battery_set_type
evidence: Stores 0xC16CE850 + 8 * type and 0xC16CE970 + 8 * type in g_battery_monitor+0 / +4 and recomputes the level at +8 from +12 in a software-pipelined loop. Called by settings_apply_all (0xC158CD68) with setting_battery_type_get(). Same code and the same 24 bytes of table data in Lofi-12 XT 1.5.205 (0xC2BCED64) and CyDrums 1.1.84 (0xC24EDE94): region_diff --data 24, only moved data addresses (run from 4 bytes earlier, which adds the previous function's final nop 4).

Tables (2026-11-10; correction: earlier evidence gave 0xC16DE850 / 0xC16DE970, a mis-decoded MVKH high half, the code builds 0xC16CE850 / 0xC16CE970 at 0xC158CBD4 / 0xC158CBE0): four u16 raw thresholds (panel channel 15) per type, type = BATTERY TYPE (PREF +0xFC, [0,2]); table +0: 0 = 2630, 2830, 2980, 3180; 1 = 2840, 2915, 2940, 2990; 2 = 3030, 3280, 3360, 3490; table +4: 0 = 2730, 2930, 3080, 3280; 1 = 2855, 2930, 2955, 3005; 2 = 3080, 3330, 3410, 3540 (each 100 / 15 / 50 above the first). Other products (2026-11-10): the same table bytes and a 0-2 validator range in Lofi-12 XT and CyDrums, but their manuals list only Alkaline and NiMH; CyDrums' parameter data has ALKALINE / NiMH / LITHIUM labels at 0xC26CA168 (packed format, not decoded). Entries 0-9 are the ten sequencer tracks' objects, set at run time: 0xC15C5490 walks them and, for an entry whose +4 field is 1 (a LOOP track), stores &g_loop_tracks[i + 10 * (bank ^ 1)] back (stw at 0xC15C5534; bank = B14+1340), so LOOP tracks switch between the two LoopTrack banks; 0xC15C5130 calls each non-null entry's vtable +8 and stores 0. The writer for the other track types was not found (inference: their VoiceTrack). Readers: audio_mix_tracks, audio_track_render, audio_mix_usb (entry 13 at 0xC16ED75C), audio_mix_ext (entry 14 at 0xC16ED760), 0xC15AAAD0, and the track accessors at 0xC15C5100-0xC15C63A4.

symbols.name: audio_mix_tracks
evidence: Called by audio_mix_main as (0xC16EFBB8, out, 0xC16DFFB0) when audio_preview_active() is 0. For each index i = 0..12 of g_track_table (the ten sequencer tracks and the three GLOBAL tracks): if the entry is set, audio_track_render(i, ...) fills g_track_dry_block and g_track_send_block; then g_track_dry_block x gain is added into out and g_track_send_block x a second gain into send (the loop at 0xC15AA520: stores through A10 = out at +16/+20/+528/+540 and through A12 = send). The gains come from the track's float at +20 and the value at B14+1008 (not resolved). A second loop (0xC15AA670, which also uses 0xC16E05C0 and 0xC16DF7A0) runs instead for the one index equal to a value saved on the stack at entry (from 0xC1611658 / 0xC158BC60; not read). After every index, set or not: the object at B14+1016, if any, gets vtable +12 (obj, entry, i, g_track_dry_block) (inference: a recording/resample tap), and audio_track_scratch_clear.
Read 2026-11-10 with the RS-fixed objdump (the compact MVs that load the gains were mis-decoded before; Ghidra agrees with the fixed listing).

symbols.name: g_control_scan
evidence: The hardware source of g_control_switch_scanner (+20): 0xC168B578-0xC168B5B4 builds it (vptr 0xC16CC190 = RTTI ControlScan vtable 0xC16CC188 + 8, +4 = 6, +8 = 8, +12 = 0) and passes it to control_switch_init. +4 = number of matrix rows (6), +8 = bits per row (8), +12 = current row, +16 = the 64-bit reading control_switch_poll merges.

symbols.name: ControlScan::scan
evidence: ControlScan vtable +4; called first by control_switch_poll. Whole body: v = gpio_read_bank16(3) (GP3 input pins); bits = GP3[1..6] -> bits 0-5, GP3[9] -> bit 6, GP3[11] -> bit 7; when the row (+12) is 0 it also reads bank 5 and sets bit 4 if GP5[10] is 0; stores the 8 bits at +16 (high word 0).

control_switch_poll then merges them as reading = (previous & ~(0xFF << 8*row)) | (bits << 8*row) (mask from +8 = 8 and +12 = row), so each poll refreshes one row of a 6 x 8 key matrix: g_control_switch_state bit n = row n / 8, column n % 8. Same code in Lofi-12 XT 1.5.205 and CyDrums 1.1.84 (region_diff with --at: 0 differences).

symbols.name: ControlScan::select_row
evidence: ControlScan vtable +8. Whole body: gpio_clr_data(1, 0x3F) (GP2[0..5] low), then gpio_set_data(1, 1 << this->row) (GP2[row] high). So the matrix rows are GP2[0..5], driven high one at a time, and the columns are read on GP3 (ControlScan::scan). Same code in Lofi-12 XT and CyDrums (region_diff: 0 differences).

symbols.name: ControlScan::reading
evidence: ControlScan vtable +20. Whole body: return the 64-bit word at this+16.

symbols.name: gpio_clr_data
evidence: Whole body: store bits to word index 0x00789807 + 10 * bank_pair, i.e. 0x01E2601C + 0x28 * bank_pair (GPIO CLR_DATA01, CLR_DATA23, ...).

symbols.name: gpio_set_data
evidence: Whole body: store bits to 0x01E26018 + 0x28 * bank_pair (GPIO SET_DATA01, SET_DATA23, ...).

symbols.name: HomeModeController::on_pad_hold
evidence: HomeModeController vtable (0xC16C5D30) slot 9, the KeyPadDelegate slot 1 that pad_hold_update fires after 60 hard samples (> 2800). Body: if the byte at B14+541 is set (0xC158B910) return 0; track = pad_to_track(pad); if 0xC151D318(track) passes, B14+1304 = pad and return 1, else B14+1304 = -2 and return 0. So the first stage only arms a pad.

Role (2026-11-10): Quick sampling. The SmplTrek 2.0.129 release notes add 'Quick sampling: by putting pressure on the track pad, you can easily record a sample'; Reference Manual v3 p. 36: on the Home Screen press down a track's pad, then REC to start and stop, then choose the track type. The hold detector's 2800 threshold (mvk 2800) is absent from 1.4.99 and present from 2.0.129. Which check 0xC151D318 makes (the manual: track type not set, or LAUNCH mode off) and what B14+541 is are not read.

symbols.name: HomeModeController::on_pad_hold_long
evidence: HomeModeController vtable slot 10, the KeyPadDelegate slot 2 that pad_hold_update fires after 180 further hard samples. Same B14+541 gate and pad_to_track / 0xC151D318 check as on_pad_hold; continues only when B14+1304 still holds this pad (armed by on_pad_hold), then calls 0xC158C0B4 and, depending on results, 0xC158BB98, 0xC1571E58, 0xC1570F60 and 0xC1668604. symbols.name: g_encoder_test_labels
evidence: Constant "ABCDV": the factory encoder test page labels encoder index 0-4 as knobs A, B, C, D and VALUE. With encoder_read_phases: A = GP3[14]/GP3[15], B = GP3[12]/GP3[10], C = GP5[2]/GP5[0], D = GP5[5]/GP5[4], VALUE = GP5[7]/GP5[8]. Note the push switches use another order (switch bit 0 = B, 1 = A, 2 = C, 3 = D, 4 = VALUE). The same string is used by Lofi-12 XT 1.5.205 (0xC2DA3160, handler 0xC2CBF1C0) and CyDrums 1.1.84 (0xC26ACF18, handler 0xC25DFCA8).

Chain checked end to end in all three (2026-11-10): encoder_poll_all hands bits (2i, 2i+1) to enc[i]; encoders_init gives enc[i] index i (compiler equivalence, see that entry and the hand files); the index reaches the page unchanged (SmplTrek dispatch_encoder B4 = msg+4; Lofi-12 XT post 0xC2BAC160 stores it at msg+4 and 0xC2C1ADC0 passes msg+4 as B4 to controller slot 6; CyDrums post 0xC24CD670 stores it at msg+4 and 0xC2546584 passes the message pointer to slot 6, whose handler reads msg+4).

Only when the mode byte at this+36 has the B14+1516 bit: write_riff_header(this, file_size - 8), write_data_header(this, (this+24) - 8, this+28) (the data byte count), then file_sync; returns 0. symbols.name: AudioEngine::WavFile::open
symbols.prototype: int AudioEngine::WavFile::open(WavFile *this, const char *path, unsigned char mode)
evidence: Read 2026-11-11. fil = file_open(path, mode) stored at this+4 and the mode byte at this+36; a null fil returns -1. The mode is tested against four flag words at B14+1512 / 1516 / 1520 / 1524 (values set at run time, not read). Create path (B14+1516 and B14+1520|1524 bits set): write_riff_header(this, 0), write_fmt_chunk(this, 12), vtable slot 2 (write extra chunks; ExpandedWavFile writes cue + LIST/labl there), write_data_header(this, file_size, 0), then this+24 = file_size (data start); returns 0 if the data header write succeeded. Read path (B14+1516 set without the create bits, or the B14+1512 bit): read_chunks(this), then file_lseek(fil, this+24) to the data start and return 0. A failed write or parse calls AudioEngine::WavFile::close and returns -1; no matching bit returns -1. (0xC1617048 / 0xC1617050 / 0xC1617060 named earlier are this function's own tail blocks, not helpers.)
AudioFileControlTask command 5 passes (stream+8, path, (u8)m2); its result 0 means opened (the task posts 1 for 0). About 30 other callers.

evidence: Allocates 556 bytes (0xC1694760 with 128; inference: an aligned heap allocation, FIL size), f_open on it, bios_free on failure. Counterpart of file_close, which frees the FIL after f_close.

symbols.name: card_free_space
evidence: f_getfree(path 0xC16BA984, &clusters, &fs), returns clusters * the 16-bit field at fs+522, shifted left by 9 into a 64-bit byte count (so the field is sectors per cluster with 512-byte sectors; inference from the shift). Lofi-12 XT 0xC2C265B8 is the same code (region_diff --at: 4 moved data addresses, 1 other).

symbols.name: card_space_check
evidence: Decoded packet by packet 2026-11-10: free = card_free_space() (64-bit bytes), x = the 32-bit argument. Returns 0 when free < 0x08000000 (128 MiB) or free < x, else 1 when free - x >= 0x08000000, else 0; i.e. 1 iff at least 128 MiB stay free after reserving x bytes. AudioFileControlTask command 0 calls it with 0 after every write block and posts an app message of type 5 when it returns 0 (less than 128 MiB free). Lofi-12 XT 0xC2BB8000 is the same code (region_diff: no differences). CyDrums has it at 0xC24E7A34 (same compares and threshold; the last two instructions, the result conversion, differ; one caller 0xC24E7AEC), but its AudioFileControlTask command 0 does not call it. SmplTrek has 15 other call sites (0xC1548F44 ... 0xC1643664), so it is a general card-space test.

symbols.name: AudioEngine::WavFile::WavFile
evidence: Stores the AudioEngine::WavFile vptr 0xC16CE6F0 (RTTI) at +0, clears +4 (FIL*), +28, +32 and more. Called by AudioEngine::ExpandedWavFile::ExpandedWavFile.

symbols.name: AudioEngine::WavFile::write

symbols.name: AudioEngine::WavFile::read

symbols.name: AudioEngine::ExpandedWavFile::ExpandedWavFile

symbols.prototype: void *afc_stream_init(void *stream, int b4, int a6, int b6)
