symbols.name: g_app_state_676
evidence: B14+676 (SmplTrek B14 0xC16F3320). An app-wide state value: written by app_state_set (about 40 call sites across the app pages, constants 0, 1, 2, 4 among others) and by 0xC1572568 (3 or 0); read by app_state_is_4 / app_state_is_2 and 3 other sites. Meaning of the values not read (name is neutral on purpose).

2026-11-14: 4 = recording a global track to the card (set by 0xC15E9C6C from AppGlobalTrackEdit's enter method after it opens two audio file streams; 0xC15E9C18 stops and sets 0). 2 is set by HomeModeController::on_pad_hold_long (mode not decoded). 1 is stored by helpers next to the Inst / Drum / Audio track edit pages, 0 by the edit pages' enter methods and the recording stop. Low space posts nothing in state 2.

Correction 2026-11-14: state 2 is quick sampling, the hard pad press added in 2.0.129 (docs/smpltrek-changelog.txt, 'Quick sampling'), set by HomeModeController::on_pad_hold_long; the note above called its mode not decoded.

symbols.name: app_state_set
evidence: Whole body: BNOP B3,4 with STW A4 -> B14+676 (g_app_state_676) in the delay slot.

symbols.name: app_state_is_4
evidence: Whole body: returns g_app_state_676 == 4.

symbols.name: app_state_is_2
evidence: Whole body: returns g_app_state_676 == 2.

symbols.name: MainDelegate::handle_app_message_5
evidence: MainDelegate primary vtable slot 13; reached for app message type 5 through MessageHandler (this+12) slot 6, the thunk 0xC15D7714 (this - 12), as MainDelegate::handle_message calls slot type+1. Switches on msg+4 (sub-codes 1-3, 5-9, 11 handled). Sub-code 2 or 3 reads msg+8: -1 goes to 0xC15D7664 / 0xC15EA0F4, -2 to 0xC15D7634 / 0xC1548C20 (a UI path that calls graphics_set_continuous); other values to 0xC154D24C. What the UI shows is not read (no string references in these functions).

2026-11-14: sub-code 2 with -1 (low space while recording a global track, state 4) reaches 0xC15EA0F4, which stops that recording and opens DialogCombineRecordedAudio (static object 0xC1503890) through 0xC1659240; with -2 it reaches 0xC1548C20, which stops and closes the active AudioFileStream (0xC1500E48) and shows no dialog.

symbols.name: file_tell
evidence: Whole body: return the word at fp+536 (index 134). f_read (0xC1509F78) validates the object at fp+512 and computes the remaining bytes as word 131 (+524) minus word 134 (+536), i.e. obj.objsize - fptr, and reads the error byte at +533. So this build's FIL has buf[512] first (FatFs R0.14 FIL members with FF_FS_LOCK's lockid after objsize: obj at 512, objsize 524, flag 532, err 533, fptr 536, size 556 = file_open's allocation). +536 is fptr: this is f_tell (a macro in FatFs).

symbols.name: file_size
evidence: Whole body: return the word at fp+524 (index 131), obj.objsize in this build's FIL layout (see file_tell): f_size.

symbols.name: AudioEngine::WavFile::write_riff_header
evidence: Builds {"RIFF" (0xC16D4460), riff_size, "WAVE" (0xC16D4468)} on the stack, file_lseek(this+4, 0), file_write of 12 bytes. Callers: AudioEngine::WavFile::open (riff_size 0) and AudioEngine::WavFile::flush (file_size - 8). Name inferred from the body.

symbols.name: AudioEngine::WavFile::write_data_header
evidence: Builds {"data" (0xC16D4450), size} on the stack, file_lseek(this+4, pos), file_write of 8 bytes. AudioEngine::WavFile::open calls it at the end of the file with size 0; AudioEngine::WavFile::flush at (this+24) - 8 with the byte count at this+28. Name inferred from the body.

symbols.name: AudioEngine::WavFile::read_riff_header
evidence: file_read of 12 bytes from this+4, compares bytes 0-3 with "RIFF" and bytes 8-11 with "WAVE" (0xC16D0BCC / 0xC16D0BD1); returns the RIFF size word on a match, 0 otherwise (also 0 on a read error). Called by AudioEngine::WavFile::read_chunks.

symbols.name: AudioEngine::WavFile::read_chunks
evidence: Returns -1 when this+4 (the FIL*) is null or read_riff_header gives 0. Then loops while file_tell < file_size - 1: reads an 8-byte chunk header; "fmt " (byte compares 'f' 'm' 't' ' ') reads 16 bytes into this+8, requires the format tag (halfword this+8) to be 1 (PCM) and skips any rest of the chunk; "data" stores the chunk size at this+28 and file_tell - (this+32) at this+24, then seeks past the data; any other chunk goes to vtable slot 3 (vptr+12) with the header, and is skipped when that returns 0. Returns 0, or -1 on a read error / non-PCM format. AudioEngine::WavFile::open calls it when opening for reading. Name inferred from the body.

symbols.name: AudioEngine::WavFile::write_fmt_chunk
evidence: Builds {"fmt " (0xC16D4420), 16, the 16 bytes at this+8} on the stack, file_lseek(this+4, pos), file_write of 24 bytes. AudioEngine::WavFile::open calls it with pos 12. So this+8 holds the 16-byte PCM format block that read_chunks fills when reading.

symbols.name: AudioEngine::ExpandedWavFile::set_tempo
evidence: BNOP B3,4 with STW B4 -> this+48 in the delay slot (0xC163A5E4 is the matching getter). Two callers (0xC156D7CC, 0xC1643570) pass project_get_tempo_x10() (0xC1611428). ExpandedWavFile::write_tempo_label prints this+48 as the label "Tempo: NNN.N".

symbols.name: AudioEngine::ExpandedWavFile::write_smpl_chunk
evidence: Builds a "smpl" (0xC16D4428) chunk on the stack (MIDI unity note 60, one sample loop), file_lseek(this+4, pos), file_write, then a 24-byte loop record with the start / end words at this+40 / this+44. The exact field layout and byte counts are not settled. No call or stored pointer to this address was found in the image (packets --calls, word scan), so it may be unused.

symbols.name: AudioEngine::ExpandedWavFile::write_cue_chunk
evidence: Builds a 36-byte "cue " (0xC16D4448) chunk, size 28: one cue point, id 1, position 0, chunk id "data" (0xC16D4440), offsets 0; file_lseek to file_size, file_write. Called by ExpandedWavFile vtable slot 2 (write_extra_chunks).

symbols.name: AudioEngine::ExpandedWavFile::write_tempo_label
evidence: Copies the template "Tempo: 120.0" (0xC16D0928) and replaces its digits with this+48 in decimal (hundreds, tens, units, tenths: divisions by 1000/100/10 through multiply-high constants). It then appends at file_size an 8-byte "LIST" (0xC16D4458) header (size 30) and a 30-byte body: "adtl" (0xC16D4438), "labl" (0xC16D4430) of size 18, cue point id 1 and the label text. Called by write_extra_chunks after write_cue_chunk.

symbols.name: AudioEngine::ExpandedWavFile::write_extra_chunks
evidence: ExpandedWavFile vtable slot 2 (0xC16CE6B0; WavFile's slot 2 is 0xC16A5580, a shared 'return 0'). Calls write_cue_chunk then write_tempo_label. AudioEngine::WavFile::open calls slot 2 after the fmt chunk when it creates a file, before the data header. So files written through ExpandedWavFile carry a cue point labelled with the tempo.

symbols.name: AudioEngine::ExpandedWavFile::read_extra_chunk
evidence: ExpandedWavFile vtable slot 3 (0xC16CE6B4; WavFile's slot 3 is 0xC16A5560, a shared 'return -1'). AudioEngine::WavFile::read_chunks passes every chunk other than fmt / data here. Compares the chunk id with "smpl", "cue " and "LIST" (string table 0xC16CE1D8 / 0xC16CE1DD / 0xC16CE1E2) and uses "data" (0xC16D4440) and "labl" (0xC16D4430). For a labl text that starts with "Tempo: " (0xC16CE1E7, 7-byte compare) it parses the digits at text offsets 7, 8, 9 and 11 as tempo x 10 into this+48, the inverse of write_tempo_label. The smpl and cue parts (36-byte header, 24-byte loop records) were not read field by field.

symbols.name: project_set_tempo_x10
evidence: BNOP B3,2 with MVK/MVKH 0xC1500CF4 and STW A4 in the delay slots. 0xC1611428 is the getter. The initialiser at 0xC1611438 stores 1200 at 0xC1500CF4 (and 100 at 0xC1500CF0). Tempo x 10 is inferred from the default 1200 and from ExpandedWavFile, which formats the getter's value as "Tempo: NNN.N" (template "Tempo: 120.0").

symbols.name: project_get_tempo_x10
evidence: Returns the word at 0xC1500CF4 (see project_set_tempo_x10). Its value is passed to AudioEngine::ExpandedWavFile::set_tempo before a file is written (0xC156D7C4, 0xC164356C).

symbols.name: MainDelegate::render_current_controller
evidence: Reads current controller at B14+860 (0xC16F367C), follows child+8 to innermost controller, dispatches vtable+48 (slot 12) at 0xC154C52E/0xC154C53A. RenderingObject thunk 0xC154C548 subtracts 52 and tail-branches here. AppSystemInfo slot 12 is 0xC15D3638, whose title slot 15 reaches 0xC1666DA0. Normal caller is the graphics task; see docs/ram-allocation.md.

symbols.name: bios_print_ring_putch
evidence: Whole sink 0xC1694DA0..0xC1694E34: length at 0xC16C6E54 (128), state at 0xC16D4D24 initialized {0xC1500718,0,0}. Save interrupt state via 0xC16AD060 -> 0xC16AD260 -> 0xC16ACB40, store byte at buffer[index], increment and wrap index/set wrapped, restore via 0xC16AD080 -> 0xC16AD280 -> 0xC16ACB60. Called by formatter output helper 0xC1694EE0; fixed RAM sink, no allocation or semaphore wait in this body. Analytical name, not library-matched.

Exact match 2026-11-14: unique 152-byte relocation-masked match to xdc_runtime_SysMin_putch__E in the prebuilt xdc.runtime library ti.targets.rts6000.ae674 / boot.ae674 shipped with SYS/BIOS 6.76.03.01 member SysMin.oe674 (analysis/lib_match.py, 2026-11-14; claim LIB-3). TI code, not Sonicware's. The name here was given from reading; TI's name is SysMin_putch.

symbols.name: project_read_temporary_buffer
evidence: Reached by 0xC158AFE0 -> 0xC162C5D4 during project selection. Opens file, reads size, allocates via 0xC1694760, initializes buffer through 0xC161B1B8, reads through 0xC1602B80, parses successful read through 0xC161B378. Observed read-success/read-failure paths call bios_free at 0xC162C594/0xC162C5A4 and file_close. Parser and error-path transitive effects are not fully audited; this is evidence of temporary allocation release, not proof against heap reset.

symbols.name: version_words_format
evidence: Writes the words v[0], v[1], v[2] (loads at +0, +4, +8) in decimal (0xC15FE2C0 with base 10 for each) separated by '.' (46). Tail-called (b with addkpc) by boot_version_string, system_version_string and preset_version_string with v = header+16. The word counterpart of version_triplet_format (bytes).

symbols.name: i2c_set_slave_address
evidence: Whole body: BNOP B3,4 with STW B4 -> *(A4+28) in the delay slot, i.e. the C6748 I2C ICSAR register (+0x1C). Callers: 0xC160C7EC (in 0xC160C78C, whose only caller is the thunk 0xC1671E90, slave 24 = 0x18 from 0xC162158C) and the tail branch at 0xC160CC28, which has no caller and no stored pointer. So the app only ever addresses I2C slave 0x18.

symbols.name: i2c_base_for_instance
evidence: Starts with B B3; the delay slots return 0x01E28000 (I2C1) when the argument is 1 and 0x01C22000 (I2C0) otherwise. Reached from i2c_open (0xC160CE04).

symbols.name: i2c_open
evidence: Per-instance state at 0xC133E048 + instance * 0x801C; if not yet open stores the instance (+4) and i2c_base_for_instance(instance) (+8), then calls the PSC enable 0xC168EC60 (PSC1 module 11 = I2C1 only when instance is 1) and three set-up helpers. Single caller: the branch at 0xC1671EB8 with drv 0xC15044AC and instance 0 (I2C0).

symbols.name: spi_base_for_instance
evidence: Returns 0x01F0E000 (SPI1) for a non-zero argument, 0x01C41000 (SPI0) for 0. Called by SPIDriver::open (0xC1626CE0) and by the SPI1 device code at 0xC15FC114 / 0xC15FC1D4 / 0xC15FC29C / 0xC15FC970 (argument 1).

symbols.name: HAL::SPIDriver::open
evidence: If this+12 is zero, stores the instance at this+4 and spi_base_for_instance(instance) as the register base used by every other SPIDriver method (this+12). Callers: 0xC167C7E8 (g_spi_driver, instance 0), 0xC167C82C (0xC15043B0, instance 1), 0xC15FC94C (0xC15043A0, instance 1).

symbols.name: HAL::SPIDriver::init
symbols.prototype: void HAL::SPIDriver::init(SPIDriver *this, uint32_t pin_mask, uint32_t bit_rate, int b6, int a8, int b8)
evidence: Returns at once when this+12 (base) is zero; otherwise resets and configures the port: the pin mask goes through 0xC167140C (SPIPC0 style: bit 0 SCS0, bit 1 SCS1, bits 9-11 CLK/SIMO/SOMI) and the bit rate to the clock set-up. Calls: g_spi_driver 0xE03 / 32 MHz (0xC167C76C), 0xC15043B0 0xE01 / 9 MHz (0xC167C79C), 0xC15043A0 0xE00 / 1453125 Hz (0xC15FC96C). Parameter meanings other than pins and rate not read.

symbols.name: HAL::SPIDriver::select
symbols.prototype: void HAL::SPIDriver::select(SPIDriver *this, int device, int assert)
evidence: SPIDriver vtable slot 0 (0xC16CF788). Passes the chip-select mask 1 << device to 0xC1671570 with the base at this+12; with assert set the flags carry bit 28 (CS hold), otherwise 0; both paths store the device at this+8. So the flash's device 0 / 1 are the SPI0 hardware chip selects SCS0 / SCS1.

symbols.name: g_spi1_driver_cs0
evidence: SPIDriver on SPI1 (open instance 1 at 0xC167C82C), pin mask 0xE01 (SCS0, CLK, SIMO, SOMI), 9 MHz. Used next to the OLED start-up code; that it carries the OLED traffic is an inference.

symbols.name: g_spi1_driver_gpio_cs
evidence: SPIDriver (vptr 0xC16CF788 set by the static constructor 0xC15FBD60) on SPI1 (open instance 1 at 0xC15FC94C), pin mask 0xE00 (no hardware chip select), 1453125 Hz. The same code takes four GPIO pins (GP7[11], GP7[12], GP7[13], GP2[15] via gpio_pin_number, kept at B14+180..192) as selects and drives the frame engine (frame_engine_init / _start / _stop): output only, and never started in 3.2.174 (see frame_engine_start). The part on those pins is not identified.

symbols.name: frame_engine_init
evidence: memset(0x11F01000, 0, 198): the frame buffer, 3 groups x 66 bytes (11 frames of 6 bytes). Then tests PINMUX5 bit 3 (0xC1690868(5) reads 0x01C14120 + 4*5). Clear: frame_engine_pinmux (0xC15FC810: PINMUX16 bits 16-27 = 0x888, PINMUX5 bits 0-3 = 8), timer 0 set-up (0xC15FC850: TGCR 0x01C20024), the four pins at B14+180..192 made outputs, GPIO bank 7 written back masked with 0xC7FF, the B14+192 pin (GP2[15]) driven low. Set: opens g_spi1_driver_gpio_cs (SPI1, pin mask 0xE00, 1453125 Hz). The only caller is the start-up code at 0xC15F37CC, which then clears g_led_state. Name inferred: it prepares the output engine but does not start it.

symbols.name: frame_engine_start
evidence: If the enable pin (B14+192, GP2[15]) reads 0: EDMA3EnableTransfer on channel 11 (Timer64P0 event 34) and channel 19 (SPI1 transmit), starts timer 0's 34 half (TCR 0x01C20020 bit 23, 0xC15FC6D8), then drives the enable pin high. No receive channel (18) is enabled, so the engine only sends. No call, branch or stored pointer reaches this address in 3.2.174 (copy-table data included) or in 1.0.65.

symbols.name: frame_engine_stop
evidence: Mirror of frame_engine_start: if the enable pin reads 1, stops timer 0's 34 half (TCR bit 23 cleared, 0xC15FC784), EDMA3DisableTransfer on channels 11 and 19, and drives the enable pin low. No caller or stored pointer.

symbols.name: frame_set_level
symbols.prototype: void frame_set_level(int group, int byte, int bit, int level)
evidence: Walks the frame buffer downwards from 0x11F01036 + group*66 + byte in 6-byte steps (one byte per frame): clears bit 'bit' in the frames from the top down to 'level' and sets it in the frames below 'level': a 10-step on-time per output, i.e. PWM brightness over the 11 frames. No caller or stored pointer.

symbols.name: frame_engine_build_chain
evidence: Builds linked EDMA PaRAM sets (EDMA3SetPaRAM 0xC15D9A64) for 3 groups x 11 frames from the buffers at 0x11F010C8 / 0x11F014E8 / 0x11F01508 / 0x11F01528, with transfers to the GPIO set / clear registers (0x01E26090 / 0x01E26094) between frames. Called only from frame_engine_start.

symbols.name: led_set
symbols.prototype: void led_set(int a, int b, int c, uint8_t value)
evidence: Index = 48a + 8b + c into g_led_state (0xC1500578), a 3 x 6 x 8 table (simulated 2026-11-13, analysis/led_callers.py; an earlier reading here said 6a + b + 8c); if the stored byte differs, stores the value and tail-calls panel_led_command(&g_ad_controller_uart, a, b, c, value). Reached through many small wrappers (0xC15F2A98 onward) and used by the AppTestLED page and ClippingLED. So the panel LEDs are driven by the panel MCU.

symbols.name: panel_led_command
symbols.prototype: void panel_led_command(ADControllerUART *uart, int a, int b, int c, int value)
evidence: Builds the 5-byte message {0xC1, a, b, c, value} on the stack and sends it with 0xC161E3C0 (this, buf, 5) over the panel-controller UART, when the call at 0xC1662BC0 on uart+28 returns non-zero. Name inferred from its callers (led_set).

symbols.name: g_led_state
evidence: Cleared (144 bytes) by the start-up code at 0xC15F37D8, right after frame_engine_init; read and written by led_set as the last value sent to the panel MCU for each LED.

symbols.name: codec_set_sample_rate
symbols.prototype: void codec_set_sample_rate(uint32_t i2c_base, int unused, int rate_hz)
evidence: AIC310x writes: reg 2 = 0, reg 3 = 0xA2 (PLL on, Q 4, P 2). rate_hz == 44100 (0xAC44): reg 4 = 28 (J 7), reg 5/6 = 54/176 (D 3500), reg 7 = 0x8A (fsref 44.1 kHz, left DAC = left, right DAC = right). Otherwise: reg 4 = 32 (J 8), reg 5/6 = 0 (D 0), reg 7 = 0x0A (fsref 48 kHz). Then reg 8 = 0xD0 (codec drives BCLK and WCLK). fsref = MCLK x K / (2048 x P) gives MCLK = 24.576 MHz for both settings (deduced; the oscillator itself is not seen).
Only caller: codec_i2c_init, with 48000 (0xBB80).

symbols.name: codec_reset
evidence: reg 0 = 0 (page 0), reg 1 = 0x80 (software reset). First call in codec_i2c_init.

symbols.name: codec_set_pll_fraction
evidence: trim >= 0: reg 4 = 32 (J 8), D = trim; trim < 0: reg 4 = 28 (J 7), D = trim + 10000; reg 5 = D bits 13..6, reg 6 = D bits 5..0 << 2. So K = 8 + trim / 10000 and the sample rate becomes 48 kHz x (1 + trim / 80000) at run time.

Reached only through the wrapper 0xC1678860, from 0xC1661080 and 0xC16612E0 next to audio_clock_probe_tick: a loop that measures Timer64P1 (0x01C21000) and steps the trim in units of 300 when the byte at B14+560 is set. What reference it follows is not traced.

symbols.name: codec_set_audio_interface
symbols.prototype: void codec_set_audio_interface(uint32_t i2c_base, int mode_bits, int word_bits, int data_offset)
evidence: reg 9 = mode_bits | word-length field (16 / 20 / 24 / 32 bits -> 0x00 / 0x10 / 0x20 / 0x30) | 7 (DAC and ADC re-sync with soft mute); reg 10 = data_offset. codec_i2c_init calls it with (0, 32, 0): reg 9 = 0x37, I2S with 32-bit words, matching mcasp_configure's 32-bit slots.

symbols.name: codec_set_dac_mute
evidence: Writes regs 43 and 44 (left / right DAC digital volume) with 0x80 (muted) or 0 (0 dB). Reached through wrapper 0xC1678640 from the power-message handlers (MainDelegate::handle_power_message, 0xC154A5CC) and from the test-audio code next to project_get_tempo_x10 (0xC16141A8, 0xC16142C0; 'SmplTrekTestAudio.wav').

symbols.name: codec_output_init
evidence: reg 37 = 0xC0 (both DACs powered), reg 41 = 0x50 (left DAC -> DAC_L3, right DAC -> DAC_R3: the direct paths to the line output drivers), reg 42 = 0x9C (output driver pop-reduction timing), reg 86 = reg 93 = 0x0B (LEFT_LOP / RIGHT_LOP: 0 dB, unmuted, powered). Last call in codec_i2c_init. No headphone (HPLOUT / HPROUT) register is written here; the headphone output path is not identified.

symbols.name: codec_route_mic3r_to_right_adc
evidence: reg 18 (MIC3L/R to right ADC) = on ? 0xF0 (MIC3R at 0 dB, MIC3L off) : 0xFF (both off).

symbols.name: codec_route_mic3r_to_left_adc
evidence: reg 17 (MIC3L/R to left ADC) = on ? 0xF0 (MIC3R at 0 dB) : 0xFF. With codec_route_mic3r_to_right_adc this feeds one MIC3R source to both ADCs (inference: the mono built-in mic).

symbols.name: codec_set_pga_right
evidence: reg 16 (right ADC PGA) = half_db & 0x7F (0.5 dB steps, bit 7 mute clear). Values seen from the gain presets: 0, 20 (10 dB), 42 (21 dB).

symbols.name: codec_set_pga_left
evidence: reg 15 (left ADC PGA) = half_db & 0x7F. Values seen from the gain presets: 0, 20 (10 dB), 42 (21 dB).

symbols.name: codec_adc_hpf_init
evidence: Selects page 1 (reg 0 = 1), writes 16-bit pairs to page-1 regs 65/66, 67/68, 69/70 and 71/72, 73/74, 75/76 (left and right ADC high-pass coefficients N0 = 32725, N1 = -32725, D1 = 32682: a first-order DC blocker with its pole at 32682/32768, about 20 Hz at 48 kHz), back to page 0, then reg 107 = 0xC0 (use the programmable filter on both ADCs). Called from codec_input_init. audio start (0xC1621574) later writes reg 12 = 0x50 through 0xC161DE80, which enables the ADC high-pass on both channels.

symbols.name: codec_input_init
evidence: reg 15 = reg 16 = 0 (ADC PGAs 0 dB), codec_adc_hpf_init, MIC3 off for both ADCs (regs 17/18 = 0xFF), reg 21 = reg 24 = 0xF8 (LINE1R -> left ADC and LINE1L -> right ADC off), reg 19 = reg 22 = 0x84 (LINE1L -> left ADC and LINE1R -> right ADC at 0 dB, fully differential, ADC channels powered; also kept in the shadow bytes 0xC1502D6D / 0xC1502D6F). Called from codec_i2c_init.

symbols.name: audio_gpio_init
evidence: Stores gpio_pin_number(bank, pin) results in B14+0..+48: GP4[12], GP4[14], GP4[15], GP4[13], GP4[10], GP2[8], GP2[9], GP1[2], GP1[3], GP7[14], GP7[15], GP5[11], GP3[8]. The setters next to it (0xC1649530 uses +44 GP5[11], 0xC16495D0 +40 GP7[15], 0xC1649580 +28, 0xC16495A8 +36 (active low), 0xC1649680 +32 (active low), 0xC1649654 +16, 0xC16496A8 +24) are called from the input-gain presets, so at least GP5[11] and GP7[15] switch analogue input stages. Pin roles beyond those two are not identified.

symbols.name: input_r_gain_apply
evidence: level 0..3 indexes the 4-entry table 0xC16F2FFC (larger values take the same preset as 0); each entry switches through 0xC15F102C to one preset: 0 and 3 -> GP5[11] off, right PGA 0 dB (0xC15F0F60); 1 -> GP5[11] on, PGA 21 dB (0xC15F0EB2); 2 -> GP5[11] on, PGA 0 dB (0xC15F0EA0). The manual's INPUT R mic gain is LOW 0 dB, NORMAL +28.8 dB, HI +50 dB; 28.8 + 21 = 49.8, so GP5[11] switches an external stage of about +28.8 dB (inference from the arithmetic).

symbols.name: input_l_gain_apply
evidence: mode 1..6 index the table 0xC16F2D30; the entries switch to presets on GP7[15] and the left PGA: GP7[15] off + 0 dB, GP7[15] on + 0 dB, GP7[15] on + 10 dB (plus a sixth entry 0xC15F11C4, not read). The manual's INPUT L Hi-Z gain is LOW 0, NORMAL +10, HI +20 dB, which fits GP7[15] = +10 dB stage plus PGA 10 dB. mode 0 takes a separate path (0xC15F1268). Which UI setting supplies mode is not traced.
